title: Power Apps: out-of-the-box Application Insights telemetry for generative pages
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the billing guidance names the Application Insights subscription, but Microsoft bills ingestion and retention through the associated Log Analytics workspace, which can be in another subscription. The required-role notes omit documented alternatives, and the categorical claims about portal-only configuration, no per-page switch and no extra telemetry credits exceed the available documentation.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn telemetry inventory does not list record content.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative pages" "Application Insights" "API" "configuration"'; opened Generate a page using natural language, including the telemetry inventory of pageViews, exceptions and dependencies; record content is not listed.

claims.claim: Azure role-based access controls govern access to Application Insights telemetry.
claims.quote: This setup provides full access to Log Analytics features, consolidates logs in one location, and allows for unified Azure role-based access control
claims.fix: Cite this Azure page and https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/manage-access. Say to review permissions on both the Application Insights resource and associated Log Analytics workspace, rather than describing only resource access.

claims.claim: This telemetry capability observes activity rather than adding autonomous business actions.
claims.quote: When you configure Application Insights data export for the environment in the Power Platform admin center, Power Apps automatically exports telemetry for published generative pages.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes, cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The telemetry destination has consumption-based Azure Monitor ingestion charges, dependent on workspace configuration.
claims.quote: the billing for data ingestion and retention is done by the workspace where the Application Insights data is located. For this reason, you can use all options of the Log Analytics pricing model, including commitment tiers, along with pay-as-you-go.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/cost-logs#application-insights-billing to sources to substantiate licensing.model: consumption and cost: variable.

claims.claim: Azure Monitor bills Application Insights data ingestion and retention.
claims.quote: Data ingestion and retention for workspace-based Application Insights resources are billed through the Log Analytics workspace where the data is located.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/create-workspace-resource for ingestion and retention billing, retaining the workspace qualification.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: closing paragraph
claims.claim: Ingestion and retention charges land in the subscription owning the Application Insights resource.
claims.quote: Data ingestion and retention for workspace-based Application Insights resources are billed through the Log Analytics workspace where the data is located. ... link it to a Log Analytics workspace in a different subscription
claims.fix: Replace both subscription statements with: 'Ingestion and retention are billed through the associated Log Analytics workspace; confirm that workspace's subscription and budget owner, as it can differ from the Application Insights resource's subscription.' Cite this page.

claims.claim: No extra Power Apps licence or credit requirement specifically for generative-page telemetry is stated.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative pages" telemetry pricing license credits cost guidance'; opened Generate a page using natural language, Export data to Application Insights, and Analyze model-driven apps and Microsoft Dataverse telemetry with Application Insights. No telemetry-specific extra rate found.
claims.fix: Qualify the absence as telemetry-specific and dated November 2026. Add the documented prerequisite that Application Insights enablement requires paid/premium Dataverse licences available for the tenant, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/analyze-telemetry.

claims.claim: Generative-page-specific telemetry cost-estimation guidance is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative pages" telemetry pricing license credits cost guidance'; opened Generate a page using natural language and Export data to Application Insights; results supplied general Azure cost guidance, not a generative-page-specific volume or pricing guide.

claims.claim: The export-creation UI is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Data export > App Insights > New data export.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... In the Manage pane, select Data export. ... On the Data export page, select the App Insights tab. Then select New data export.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Application Insights data export is supported for Managed Environments only.
claims.quote: This feature is turned on and supported for managed environments only.

claims.claim: Configuring export needs the Power Platform administrator role.
claims.quote: being assigned to the Power Platform administrator or Dynamics 365 administrator role at the tenant-level in Microsoft Entra ID
claims.fix: Replace 'Needs Power Platform admin' with 'Requires Power Platform administrator or Dynamics 365 administrator at tenant level', retaining the separate environment-role requirement. Apply to front matter and rendered table.

claims.claim: Configuring export needs the System Administrator role in the environment.
claims.quote: and by being assigned to the environment administrator or system administrator role within the Dataverse environment. Without these permissions, the integration doesn't work.
claims.fix: Replace the environment-role clause with 'and environment administrator or system administrator within the Dataverse environment'. Apply to front matter and rendered table; retain both tenant and environment role requirements.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for configuring this Power Platform environment export is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Power Platform Application Insights data export API PowerShell export package portal only' and '"Application Insights" "data export" "Power Platform" "PowerShell" configure'; opened Export data to Application Insights. No equivalent found; Azure continuous export is a different operation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a UI or API telemetry switch for an individual generative page.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative pages" "telemetry" "disable" "page"' and '"generative pages" "Application Insights" "API" "configuration"'; opened Generate a page using natural language and Export data to Application Insights. No per-page switch found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second row; Open questions
claims.claim: There is no per-page telemetry setting.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative pages" "telemetry" "disable" "page"'; opened Generate a page using natural language and Export data to Application Insights. Neither states that a per-page setting does not exist.
claims.fix: Change the note to 'Telemetry follows the environment export; Microsoft has not documented a per-page UI or API switch as of November 2026.' Keep the open question about disabling individual pages; do not answer it categorically in the note.

claims.claim: The export is portal-only.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Power Platform Application Insights data export API PowerShell export package portal only'; opened Export data to Application Insights. It documents the portal, not an exclusive portal-only restriction.
claims.fix: Replace 'The export is portal-only' with 'Microsoft documents portal configuration; an equivalent automation interface is not yet documented as of November 2026.'

claims.where: Governance controls: closing paragraph; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Azure daily caps and retention settings are relevant cost controls for the exported Application Insights telemetry.
claims.quote: You should configure the daily cap setting for both Application Insights and Log Analytics to limit the amount of telemetry data ingested by your service. For workspace-based Application Insights resources, the effective daily cap is the minimum of the two settings.
claims.fix: Cite this page and https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/create-workspace-resource. Specify both Application Insights and workspace daily caps, with retention on the associated workspace; avoid implying a daily cap is a guaranteed spend ceiling.

claims.claim: The generative pages feature itself needs no extra credits.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative pages" telemetry pricing license credits cost guidance'; opened Generate a page using natural language. FAQ: 'the maker experience for generative pages (and plans) don't require any additional AI or message credits'. No equivalent statement for telemetry runtime found.
claims.fix: Replace the final cost-rationale sentence with 'Microsoft has not published a telemetry-specific Power Apps credit requirement as of November 2026.' If retaining the FAQ, explicitly limit it to the maker experience.

claims.claim: Admins and developers can use Application Insights to monitor published generative pages.
claims.quote: Admins and developers can monitor published generative pages with Application Insights.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to set telemetry retention and access and build exception alerts, but the controls table has no corresponding rows.
claims.quote: 'Set retention and access for the telemetry'; 'Build alerts on exceptions for critical pages'. The table contains only environment export and an undocumented per-page telemetry switch.
claims.fix: Add sourced controls rows for workspace retention, telemetry access and exception alerts. Also represent the daily-cap control named in the closing paragraph, using Microsoft-documented UI paths or automation references.
